mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is always active and does not require threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% signals weak labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through joint deterioration in demand and supply.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both decline from 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO decline, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL above 3.0% annualized), the S&P 500 underperforms due to reduced liquidity and higher real rates, with the signal active when FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% in 6 months and CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rise > 0.5% in 6 months AND CPIAUCSL > 3.0
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during the tightening regime, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. This mechanism is always active and does not require threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS exceeds 140,000 thousand, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, a leading indicator of economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST is below 1400, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.0%) indicates a stagflationary environment, which is associated with negative equity returns through joint pressure on growth and inflation, requiring both conditions to be met.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5 and UNRATE > 6.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (indicating contraction) signals an imminent economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced manufacturing activity.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO is below 100 during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
